_comment: One row per reference mode run by run-mode.sh. mode: the lobby's Mode select value (client/main.js modeSel: {t:'mode', v}); map: the lobby's Map select ({t:'map', name}), null keeps the room's (server.js: 'default', Horde picks the first map with defender spawns, Tutorial its own map, World generates one); ai: Add AI presses; guest: a second native client seated as a player (Spanish); teams: the host's Team selects per seat in seat order (host, guest, AIs); capturePlay: the natives send their army at the points they do not hold (-TCCapturePlay); drive: the natives play the Tutorial from their own snapshots (-TCTutorialDrive); cap: seconds of match after which the run stops waiting; the host ends the match at the cap (server.js 'end') when the mode's own end has not come; capReason says why it cannot come within a run; shots: match seconds of the mid-match captures. Authored scenarios (shared/scenarios.js migrateScenario: maps with legacy triggers) are Conquest matches on their maps.

assault.note: the natives defend (defender team 0, the lobby default); the AI attacks; the clock is 900 s

annihilation-sandbox.note: Annihilation with the lobby's Sandbox on: 30 s in, the host picks the Kaiju in the sandbox panel (side Enemy, the default: shared/sim.js sandboxSpawn gives it to the first rival, the AI) and spawns four by its own HQ, so the natives' bunkers can fall within a run (the plain run ended at its 1500 s cap with every bunker standing); no supply truck

horde.note: the host presses Send next wave at every break (server.js 'nextwave'), as a host who wants the waves sooner

horde-sandbox.note: Horde with the lobby's Sandbox on: after wave 1 starts the host picks the Kaiju in the sandbox panel (side Enemy, the default) and spawns four for the Horde (round 15 run B's steps), so the bunker falls within the run; no supply truck

tutorial.note: both seats play (-TCTutorialDrive): the host in English, rendered; the guest in Spanish, headless, as a player (seat 1), logging its own orders per step

tutorial-es.note: as tutorial, with the Spanish guest rendered too so its step captures exist (tutorial-es-step-N-of-9); needs GPU memory for two rendered clients

world.capReason: World Conquest is won by owning a share of a generated continent's regions or by outlasting every rival nation; neither is reachable by an AI against two idle seats within a verification run, so the host ends the match at the cap (server.js 'end')

scenario-the-great-bridge.capReason: the scenario's own script (wired at 300 s, warned at 400 s, blown at 420 s, match ticks) is what this run plays: the two natives sit on opposite teams and nobody captures, so the Conquest end cannot come and the host ends the match at 480 s. With an AI in the match the points were won at 5 min 29 s (natives capturing, run -r) and 5 min 20 s (AI capturing, run -r5), both before the warning and the blow; those runs are the scenario's end-to-end rows
scenario-the-great-bridge.note: the captures sit 6 s after each event (the driver's clock starts with the play state about 2 s before tick 0); a rendered native spectator flies the tour over the bridge before the warning, at it and after the blow (tours/the-great-bridge.tour): the seats' own captures keep the intact bridge, because a seat only learns of terrain its units see (shared/sim.js observedTerrainFor) and nobody went near it (run -b5t)
